preamble: Proto-Indo-European voiced aspirated *bʰ became the voiceless fricative /f/ in Proto-Italic, probably through a voiceless aspirate and bilabial fricative stage (*bʰ > *pʰ > *ɸ > f). Latin keeps f only word-initially (medially it has b, as in albus 'white'), while the Osco-Umbrian languages show f in medial position too (Umbrian alfu 'white'). Greek reached [f] only indirectly, via *pʰ (φ), so it belongs to p_aspirated_to_f. The direct correspondence is restricted to Italic.

examples.note: Osco-Umbrian has f also word-internally, where Latin has b (albus).

sources: de Vaan, M. (2008). Etymological Dictionary of Latin and the other Italic Languages. Brill.
Sihler, A. L. (1995). New Comparative Grammar of Greek and Latin. Oxford University Press.
